title: Dual Koszul cohomology below the top degree
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let $K^\vee$ be its signed dual cochain Koszul complex [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex]. For every $n\in\mathbb N$ with $n<r$, the module $H^n(K^\vee)$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, local signed dual Koszul computation; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQZ

proof.text: Obtain the regularity-free signed complementary term equivalences e_j and commuting differential squares. This is the first, algebraic part of the source argument, without passing to homology.

For 0<n<r, Koszul regularity makes K exact in the positive degree r-n. If x is a dual cocycle, its image e_n(x) is a Koszul cycle by the commuting square in degree n. Exactness gives a preimage y in K_(r-n+1). Its preimage under e_(n-1) is a dual cochain whose boundary is x by the commuting square in degree n-1 and injectivity of e_n. Use the ModuleCat elementwise exactness criterion to conclude exactness, then zero homology. Natural-number predecessor and successor identities follow from n<r.

For n=0, r>0 and regularity makes K exact at r. The commuting square sends a dual degree-zero cocycle x to a degree-r Koszul cycle. Any incoming witness lies in wedge^(r+1) A^r, which is zero: its exterior basis is indexed by (r+1)-element subsets of Fin r, an empty type. Thus e_0(x)=0 and injectivity gives x=0, establishing dual exactness at zero. When r=0 no n<r exists; no nontriviality hypothesis was used.

based_on.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext, local signed dual Koszul computation; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BQZ

proof_origin.note: Lean proves exactness and vanishing by elementwise transport along the degreewise complementary equivalences. The zero-degree boundary is proved from the empty exterior basis; only construction and differential compatibility of the signed equivalences remain a new item.
